summary: PLAN-TO-LEAD retrospective for SD-LEO-INFRA-AUTOMATED-VENTURE-TROUBLESHOOTING-001: FR-1 through FR-6 delivered under chairman ratification 1afdeaac, split across two repos (EHG_Engineer PR #8675, altifyai PR #95) per an explicit LEAD scope-lock. Handoff scores LEAD-TO-PLAN 96 / PLAN-TO-EXEC 92 / EXEC-TO-PLAN 88. SECURITY needed three iterative passes to close real credential-redaction gaps in a brand-new external-log-handling module before reaching PASS; the Cloudflare Workers Observability telemetry API contract had to be corrected against this codebase's own live-verified reader rather than trusted from documentation. Both PRs open at handoff time: EHG_Engineer CI running, altifyai CI passing per SECURITY's own check.
recommendations: LEAD final approval should confirm both PR #8675 (EHG_Engineer) and PR #95 (altifyai) reach green CI before closing the SD -- EHG_Engineer CI was still running as of this handoff.

Formally resolve spec-conflict signal b9787bf4 (QF-20260906-986 vs pinned altifyai tests TS-10/TS-12) rather than leaving the FR-4 composeFailureDetail cut as an implicit deferral -- the cause now travels via FR-1's captured D1/log evidence instead, but the conflict itself was never closed, only routed around at LEAD scope-lock.

Capture the credential-redaction checklist SECURITY enforced here (word-boundary regex against compound env-var names, base64 alphabet coverage for base64URL/JWTs, explicit Basic-auth handling) as a reusable pre-check for any future module that ingests raw external log or credential content, rather than rediscovering it per-SD via FAIL cycles.

When a PRD depends on an external API's real request/response shape, require a citation to a live-verified reader/caller already in the codebase (as altifyai's scripts/query-observability-logs.mjs, QF-20260819-687, was here) before PLAN accepts the PRD's contract description -- this SD's first-pass guess from documentation alone was wrong.
detailed_analysis: Scope: LEAD applied a 25% scope-lock reduction at the nine-question gate -- cutting FR-4's composeFailureDetail redacted-message-prefix half (collided with pinned altifyai security tests TS-10/TS-12; diagnosis instead travels via FR-1's captured D1 rows and Worker log capture, and the console.error failure_code line had already shipped in altifyai #94), and reducing FR-2/FR-3 to invoke the already-shipped one-shot workflows (one-shot-secret-provision.yml #90, one-shot-d1-query.yml #91) with fail-loud wiring rather than authoring new provisioning logic. Delivery split cleanly along the LEAD-locked repo boundary: EHG_Engineer PR #8675 carries FR-1 (captured_cause walker: lib/apa/venture-cause-capture.js, lib/uat/result-recorder.js, lib/apa/journey-walk-orchestrator.js) and FR-5 (status-line surfacing: lib/governance/venture-cause-line.js, venture-build-status.mjs, lib/fleet/parent-completion.mjs); altifyai PR #95 carries FR-2 (deploy.yml secret provisioning via scripts/ci/provision-forwarding-secrets.sh), FR-3 (token-scope check via scripts/ci/check-cloudflare-token-scope.mjs), FR-4 reduced (capture.js console.error flip only), and FR-6 (doc rewrite). Sub-agent evidence trail across phases: LEAD ran VALIDATION/RISK/TESTING-prospective/Explore (all CONDITIONAL_PASS or PASS); PLAN ran DESIGN/DATABASE/TESTING; EXEC ran TESTING (measured: 2403 tests passed) and SECURITY across three passes -- initial FAIL on SEC-1/SEC-2/SEC-5/SEC-6 (credential-redaction gaps in the new Cloudflare-log-capture module), fixed, re-FAIL on SEC-6 alone (Basic-auth gap missed in the first fix), fixed again, final PASS. Each SECURITY pass closed exactly the finding it raised -- no scope drift, no re-opened prior findings. The most consequential technical correction: the Cloudflare Workers Observability telemetry query API's real shape (epoch-millisecond timeframe, a queryId/parameters.datasets/parameters.filters request body, and result.events.events as the authoritative response path with a same-shaped result.events.series decoy) was first guessed incorrectly from documentation and had to be corrected against altifyai's own already-existing, live-verified reader (scripts/query-observability-logs.mjs, delivered under QF-20260819-687) -- the producer's real measured output was the ground truth documentation could not substitute for.

retrospective.title: SD-LEO-INFRA-AUTOMATED-VENTURE-TROUBLESHOOTING-001 -- PLAN-TO-LEAD retrospective
retrospective.quality_score_basis: Rubric from scripts/generate-comprehensive-retrospective.js calculateQualityScore: base 70 + sub-agent verification >=3 distinct codes across phases (+10) + achievements list >=5 items (+5) + learnings list >=5 items (+5) = 90. Distinct from the pre-existing generic SD_COMPLETION retrospective (id 77a5dcd2-ad3f-477d-9fbe-9a53c009b4f4, quality_score 80, auto-generated) which this row supplements with handoff-specific real evidence rather than replaces -- that row is protected by this repo's retro-clobber-guard (retro_type=SD_COMPLETION, status=PUBLISHED, quality_score>=70) and was intentionally left untouched.
success_patterns: LEAD's 9-question scope-lock gate cut 25% of original scope (FR-4's composeFailureDetail half, FR-2/FR-3 reduced to reuse already-shipped one-shot workflows) before EXEC started, avoiding duplicated provisioning logic and a collision with pinned altifyai security tests TS-10/TS-12.

Cross-repo delivery was split at LEAD with an explicit rule (one PR per repo; the altifyai PR URL attached as EXEC evidence since this repo's gates cannot see the altifyai repo) rather than discovered ad hoc during EXEC.

SECURITY's three-pass cycle on the new Cloudflare-log-capture module closed exactly the finding each pass raised (SEC-1/2/5/6 -> fixed -> SEC-6 re-FAIL -> fixed -> PASS) with no scope drift and no re-opened prior findings.
TESTING measured 2403 passing tests at EXEC-TO-PLAN with zero regressions, consistent with the SD's own success-criteria target.
failure_patterns: The Cloudflare Workers Observability telemetry query API's real request/response shape (epoch-ms timeframe, queryId/parameters.datasets/parameters.filters body, result.events.events as authoritative with a same-shaped result.events.series decoy) was initially guessed incorrectly from documentation rather than verified against the codebase's own live-verified reader from the start.

The first SECURITY pass missed a Basic-auth handling gap (SEC-6) that only surfaced on re-FAIL after the first round of fixes -- the initial fix pass was not exhaustive against the full credential-redaction surface (word-boundary regex, base64 alphabet, auth-scheme coverage) in one attempt.
Spec-conflict signal b9787bf4 (QF-20260906-986 vs TS-10/TS-12) was routed around via a scope cut at LEAD rather than formally resolved -- the conflict itself remains open.

key_learnings.learning: Reading the producer's real measured output (altifyai's scripts/query-observability-logs.mjs, QF-20260819-687, an already-existing live-verified reader for the Cloudflare Workers Observability telemetry query API) beats re-deriving an API contract from documentation -- the epoch-millisecond timeframe, queryId/parameters.datasets/parameters.filters body shape, and the result.events.events-vs-result.events.series decoy were only caught by reading the existing caller's real output, not by reading Cloudflare's docs.
key_learnings.applicability: When a PRD's PLAN phase depends on an external API's request/response shape, require a citation to an existing live-verified caller in the codebase before accepting the contract description.

key_learnings.learning: SECURITY caught real, non-hypothetical credential-redaction gaps in a brand-new module handling raw external log content: word-boundary regex failing on compound env-var names, a base64 alphabet not covering base64URL/JWTs, and no Basic-auth handling at all. Three iterative passes were needed (FAIL on SEC-1/2/5/6 -> fixed -> re-FAIL on SEC-6 -> fixed -> PASS), each closing exactly the finding raised.
key_learnings.applicability: Any new module ingesting raw external log/credential content should be checked against this same three-gap class (compound-name word boundaries, base64URL/JWT alphabet, auth-scheme coverage) proactively rather than discovering it via sequential SECURITY FAILs.

key_learnings.learning: LEAD's 25% scope-lock reduction kept delivered scope aligned with already-proven infrastructure: FR-2/FR-3 were reduced from 'new provisioning logic' to 'invoke the already-shipped one-shot workflows (one-shot-secret-provision.yml #90, one-shot-d1-query.yml #91) with fail-loud wiring', and FR-4's composeFailureDetail half was cut entirely because it collided with pinned altifyai tests TS-10/TS-12.
key_learnings.applicability: Before PLAN authors new implementation logic, check LEAD's 9-question deletion audit (q8) for scope already reducible to invoking existing shipped one-shot workflows.

key_learnings.learning: This SD's deliverables spanned two repositories (EHG_Engineer and rickfelix/altifyai). LEAD recorded an explicit target_repo_split rule at scope-lock time (one PR per repo; altifyai PR URL attached as EXEC evidence since EHG_Engineer's own gates cannot see the altifyai repo; EXEC branches altifyai from fresh origin/main since local checkouts were 132 commits behind).
key_learnings.applicability: Cross-repo SDs should record the repo split and PR-attachment rule at LEAD scope-lock, not leave it for EXEC to discover, since the gate pipeline in one repo cannot validate evidence that only exists in the other.

action_items.text: Confirm EHG_Engineer PR #8675 reaches green CI (was still running at handoff time) before LEAD final approval closes the SD.
Formally resolve spec-conflict signal b9787bf4 (QF-20260906-986 vs TS-10/TS-12) rather than leaving it as an implicit scope-lock deferral.

Document the three-gap credential-redaction checklist (word-boundary compound-name regex, base64URL/JWT alphabet, Basic-auth coverage) as a reusable SECURITY pre-check for future modules that ingest raw external log content.
Require citation of an existing live-verified reader/caller in the codebase when a PRD depends on an external API's request/response contract, before PLAN accepts that contract description.
